findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done — New evidence beyond the earlier settled finding: when an upstream change causes another review of the same task HEAD, `review._history` keys results by commit and replaces the older result (review.py:583–594). The new `$accepted` block is built only from that history, not the item's `known` list. After two such rereviews, a below-bar or owner-accepted finding from the first review is absent from the third prompt, so it can be raised again despite item 3's carry-forward rule.
findings.title: Disputed keep settled-context carry-forward: same-commit rereviews lose earlier accepted findings

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Not done — New evidence beyond the earlier below-bar fix: `held` remains true for a scored note at the bar even after it has a `Disposition: keep` line. This condition therefore treats a disposed Harm 3 note as open. With three blocked read rounds and a coordinator-disposed at-bar Harm 3 note, the next `forge read` still refuses at the loop stop, although item 4 limits that stop to open Harm 3 notes or an at-bar `Disputed keep`.
